takeaways: Market leadership is rotating away from hyperscalers as Big Tech's massive AI capital expenditures pressure free cash flow, favoring value-oriented sectors and broader index participation.
Global economic growth is cooling, with China’s domestic demand faltering and Hong Kong’s momentum moderating, even as geopolitical tensions drive energy volatility and accelerate EV adoption.

Investors are shifting focus from AI hype to tangible financial results and infrastructure efficiency, while rising bond yields and regulatory scrutiny create a more challenging valuation environment.

items.title: Gold Erases Early Rally as WGC Reports First-Half Central Bank Buying at Lowest Since 2022
bullets: Central bank gold buying has hit its slowest first-half pace since 2022, with Russia emerging as a significant seller by offloading 22 tonnes to finance budget deficits.
The market is shifting toward two-way flows as central banks increasingly utilize gold reserves to manage currency volatility and support fiscal needs, moving away from consistent net accumulation.
items.reason: Signals a major shift in central bank reserve management strategies.

items.title: RBI set to hold rates even as global peers pivot to hikes amid inflation risks
bullets: The Reserve Bank of India is expected to maintain current interest rates despite a global trend toward tightening, as domestic inflation remains within manageable levels.
This policy divergence highlights India's resilience to external oil shocks, though the central bank remains cautious regarding the impact of global supply chain disruptions on local price stability.
items.reason: Highlights significant monetary policy divergence in emerging markets.

items.title: How M’East crisis narrows CBN’s options in fighting inflation
bullets: The Central Bank of Nigeria is facing a 'higher-for-longer' interest rate environment as Middle East instability threatens to exacerbate imported inflation through energy price volatility.

Policy makers are prioritizing exchange rate stability and increased crude oil production as primary levers to mitigate external shocks, signaling a move toward structural rather than purely monetary solutions.
items.reason: Illustrates the transmission of geopolitical risk to emerging market monetary policy.

items.title: Here's the single biggest reason the bull market is broadening
bullets: Aggressive capital expenditure by Big Tech to fund AI ambitions is suppressing free cash flow, prompting a rotation of investor interest toward value-oriented sectors and small-cap stocks.
For the first time since 2009, the equally weighted S&P 500 has outperformed the market-cap-weighted index by over 7.3%, signaling a significant shift in market leadership away from hyperscalers.
items.reason: Explains the structural shift in market leadership and sector rotation.

items.title: SpaceX's post-IPO plunge sets tense backdrop for first earnings report
bullets: SpaceX faces a critical earnings debut with its stock down 50% from all-time highs, compounded by an upcoming August 6 lockup expiration that could flood the market with insider shares.

Analysts project massive capital requirements, with debt expected to grow fivefold to over $218 billion by 2028, raising concerns about the long-term return on investment for its AI and satellite infrastructure.
items.reason: High-profile IPO earnings event with significant supply-side risks and capital intensity concerns.

items.title: Bond Market Signals Growing Risks for Stocks
bullets: The 10-year Treasury yield remains near multi-year highs while the 30-year yield has breached 5%, creating significant headwinds for corporate profitability and consumer borrowing costs.

While credit spreads remain tight, the bond market is signaling a more challenging environment for equity valuations as investors demand higher compensation for the risks associated with persistent economic uncertainty.
items.reason: Highlights the direct transmission of rising long-term yields to equity market valuations.

items.title: Global Market: Euro zone bond yields decline as falling oil prices boost market sentiment
bullets: German 10-year yields retreated 5 basis points to 3.158% as lower oil prices eased inflation expectations, directly impacting central bank policy outlooks.
Money markets have adjusted their expectations for European Central Bank tightening, now pricing in 41 basis points of future hikes compared to 44 basis points at the end of last week.
items.reason: Demonstrates the sensitivity of European sovereign debt to energy-driven inflation expectations.

items.title: How likely is Beijing to walk the talk on boosting consumption?
bullets: China's second-quarter GDP growth decelerated to 4.3%, dragging the first-half average to 4.7% and barely maintaining the official annual target range of 4.5-5%.

Domestic demand is faltering, evidenced by a 5.7% decline in fixed-asset investment, an 18% plunge in property investment, and a sharp slowdown in retail sales growth to just 0.2% in the second quarter.
items.reason: Signals significant structural weakness in China's primary growth drivers.

items.title: The World Should Not Ignore China’s Undervalued Currency
bullets: China's current account surplus is estimated to be 6% of GDP when adjusted for gold imports and misreported investment income, suggesting the renminbi is undervalued by 30-35%.

The People's Bank of China is actively intervening in currency markets, reportedly buying approximately $50 billion in foreign currency monthly to prevent renminbi appreciation and maintain export competitiveness.
items.reason: Highlights potential for increased trade tensions and currency manipulation scrutiny.

items.title: Hong Kong: Growth seen moderating – UOB
bullets: Hong Kong's GDP growth decelerated to 4.3% year-on-year in 2Q26, with a 0.6% quarterly contraction marking the first decline since 4Q22 as economic momentum cools.

While electronics exports remain supported by the global AI cycle, UOB maintains a cautious outlook with 2026 GDP growth forecast at 3.9%, citing downside risks from geopolitical uncertainty and tighter capital controls.
items.reason: Macroeconomic data indicating a shift in growth trajectory.

items.title: Zhongji Innolight listing is largest Hong Kong IPO since 2019
bullets: Optical module leader Zhongji Innolight raised HKD53.41 billion in its dual listing, marking the largest IPO on the HKEX since 2019 and signaling potential renewed interest in the exchange.

The offering attracted 33 high-profile cornerstone investors including BlackRock, JP Morgan Asset Management, and major tech firms, underscoring strong institutional confidence in AI-related infrastructure plays.
items.reason: Significant capital market activity and liquidity event for the HKEX.

items.title: Big Tech Results Show 'Mixed Shocks,' Market Direction Uncertain
bullets: Market sentiment is increasingly bifurcated, as evidenced by Microsoft's record $450 billion single-day market cap gain contrasted with Apple's 7.4% decline following weak quarterly forecasts.
Investors are shifting focus from broad AI hype to tangible financial results, penalizing companies like Meta for rising infrastructure costs that threaten near-term free cash flow.
items.reason: Divergent earnings results are driving significant volatility and re-evaluations of AI-heavy tech portfolios.

items.title: Australia ups demands on Big Tech firms to pay for news stories
bullets: Australia is set to introduce legislation imposing a 2.5% levy on digital advertising revenue for major platforms like Google, Meta, and LinkedIn if they fail to secure commercial content deals with local publishers.

While the levy rate has increased from 2.25%, the government narrowed the scope to apply only to digital advertising revenue rather than total local revenue, potentially limiting the financial impact on tech giants.
items.reason: Regulatory pressure on tech ad revenue models is intensifying globally, creating new compliance costs and operational risks.

items.title: Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) foundry roadmaps — breaking down TSMC, Intel, Samsung, and GlobalFoundries' approach to next-generation scale-up connectivity
bullets: As AI cluster bandwidth requirements exceed the capabilities of traditional electrical interconnects, the industry is shifting toward Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) to maintain performance at 200-400 Gb/s per lane.

CPO technology reduces power consumption and increases bandwidth density by moving optical engines directly onto the processor package, creating a critical new infrastructure layer for major semiconductor foundries like TSMC and Intel.
items.reason: Highlights a critical hardware bottleneck and infrastructure shift for AI scaling.

items.title: US scrutinizing Anthropic's artificial intelligence training methods
bullets: The U.S. government is initiating scrutiny into the training methodologies of leading AI developer Anthropic, signaling a potential increase in regulatory oversight for foundation model development.

Increased federal investigation into proprietary training data and processes poses significant operational and legal risks for high-profile AI firms, potentially impacting future model deployment and capital allocation.
items.reason: Regulatory intervention in top-tier AI labs is a major market-moving risk factor.

items.title: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited (TSM): An Unmatched Technological Lead in Semiconductors
bullets: Fundsmith Equity Fund has initiated a new position in TSMC, citing its dominant 90% market share in advanced semiconductor manufacturing as a critical 'moat' against competitors.

The investment firm highlights that the $20 billion capital requirement to construct a single advanced factory creates a significant barrier to entry, reinforcing TSMC's long-term growth potential in the AI infrastructure sector.
items.reason: Institutional endorsement of TSMC's competitive moat.

items.title: Samsung SDS launches NPU-as-a-Service offering with FuriosaAI chips in South Korea
bullets: Samsung SDS has launched South Korea's first NPU-as-a-Service (NPUaaS) using FuriosaAI's 5nm RNGD accelerators, which provide 512 teraflops of FP8 compute per unit for agentic AI workloads.

The service allows enterprises to access high-performance AI inference infrastructure via the Samsung Cloud Platform without the capital expenditure of managing dedicated hardware, potentially lowering total cost of ownership.
items.reason: Emergence of alternative AI inference infrastructure models.

items.title: Price war fears grip China’s EV market after woeful July sales figures
bullets: Major premium EV manufacturers Xpeng, Nio, and Li Auto all reported month-on-month sales declines in July, signaling a potential cooling of demand in the world's largest EV market.

The synchronized downturn across key players has heightened investor anxiety regarding a return to aggressive price-cutting strategies, which could further compress profit margins across the Chinese automotive sector.
items.reason: Signals potential margin compression and cooling demand in a critical global market.

items.title: Mideast war supercharges electric car sales
bullets: The International Energy Agency reported a 35% surge in global EV sales during the second quarter, directly attributed to fuel price volatility and energy security concerns stemming from Middle East geopolitical tensions.
While the broader automotive market is projected to decline in 2026, the IEA expects EV sales to grow by 10% annually, now accounting for nearly 30% of total global vehicle sales.
items.reason: Highlights a significant macroeconomic driver shifting consumer behavior toward EVs.

items.title: Substrate AI establishes data center REIT to accelerate investments in AI infrastructure
bullets: Substrate AI has launched a SOCIMI (REIT) to decouple its real estate assets from core technology operations, creating a dedicated vehicle to attract institutional capital for high-performance computing infrastructure.

The move reflects a broader industry trend of spinning off stabilized assets into REIT structures to manage the massive capital requirements of AI-scale data centers while facilitating future project financing.
items.reason: Strategic shift in capital structure for AI infrastructure.

items.title: Empromptu AI Launches Grid Guard to Stop AI Data Centers From Breaking Their Own Power Infrastructure
bullets: Empromptu AI's new 'Grid Guard' software reduces power volatility by 80% by staggering GPU workloads, potentially lowering the massive capital expenditure currently required for overbuilding backup power systems.

By smoothing millisecond-level power spikes, the technology addresses a critical operational bottleneck that threatens grid stability and increases the risk of costly service-level agreement breaches in high-density AI facilities.
items.reason: Technological solution to high-cost AI power volatility.

items.title: FAA proposal eyes fewer regulations for rocket launches, sparking concerns
bullets: The FAA has proposed a new rule that would allow the agency to waive major environmental and historic preservation regulations, including the National Environmental Policy Act and the Clean Water Act, for commercial space licensing.

This regulatory shift aims to streamline the approval process for the rapidly increasing frequency of commercial launches, potentially reducing operational hurdles for major industry players like SpaceX and Blue Origin.
items.reason: Significant regulatory shift impacting operational costs and timelines for the entire commercial space sector.

items.title: Rocket Lab Lands Launch Contract, Space Force Taps Vendors For $981 Million Program
bullets: The U.S. Space Force has awarded contracts totaling $981 million to various vendors, signaling continued aggressive government spending on orbital launch capabilities and space-based infrastructure.

Rocket Lab's inclusion in these high-value government contracts highlights the growing diversification of the launch market beyond incumbents, providing a critical revenue stream for smaller, publicly traded aerospace firms.
items.reason: Direct evidence of substantial government capital allocation into the competitive launch services market.
